title: Recovering Readout-Limited Fisher Information in Superconducting-Qubit Magnetometry with Squeezed Microwaves
authors: M. -R. Yun, Y. -J. Qu, Zheng Shan, L. -L. Yan, Yu Jia, S. -L. Su
abstract: The performance of superconducting-qubit magnetometers depends not only on magnetic-field encoding during Ramsey interrogation, but also on how efficiently the encoded information is recovered during readout. Here we quantify how squeezed-microwave-assisted dispersive readout can recover magnetic-field information lost during qubit-state assignment. We develop an effective detected-mode framework linking projected quadrature noise, state-assignment error, and the classical Fisher information accessible from binary readout outcomes. A finite mismatch between the squeezed quadrature and the discrimination axis produces an optimal squeezing strength through the competition between squeezed and anti-squeezed fluctuations. For representative parameters, squeezed readout reduces the readout-limited magnetic-field sensitivity bound by $27.3\%$. This improvement arises from recovering information lost in the readout stage rather than from increasing the information encoded during Ramsey interrogation. These results may provide a practical route for mitigating measurement-stage information loss in superconducting quantum sensing.
summary: This paper analyzes superconducting-qubit magnetometry, focusing on how readout noise limits the achievable magnetic-field sensitivity. By developing a framework linking readout noise to the classical Fisher information, the authors show that applying squeezed microwaves can recover significant amounts of lost information. This results in a measurable improvement in sensor sensitivity, offering a practical path for quantum sensing.
main_problem: The paper quantifies how using squeezed microwaves during the readout process can recover magnetic-field information lost during the state assignment stage in superconducting-qubit magnetometry.
main_result: Squeezed readout can reduce the readout-limited magnetic-field sensitivity bound by 27.3% by recovering information lost during measurement, rather than by improving the initial encoding.
method: The authors develop an effective detected-mode framework linking projected quadrature noise, state-assignment error, and the classical Fisher information accessible from binary readout outcomes.
model_or_system: The system is a superconducting-qubit magnetometer using flux-tunable transmon qubits coupled to a microwave resonator (Circuit QED). The analysis involves modeling the dispersive readout process and incorporating quantum noise reduction via squeezing.
key_observables: Readout-limited magnetic-field sensitivity bound ($\eta_{RL}^B$), Classical Fisher Information ($F_C$), projected quadrature noise ($V_j$), and state-assignment error ($	ext{perr}$).
important_parameters: Squeezing strength ($r$), quadrature mismatch angle ($	heta_j$), and the coupling/detuning parameters of the circuit QED setup.
main_assumptions: The analysis models the readout process using the quantum Langevin equation and assumes the dispersive regime for the qubit-resonator interaction.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the magnetometry principle, showing how imperfect readout broadens the likelihood function, and demonstrate the reduction in sensitivity and recovery of Fisher information using squeezing.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the magnetometry protocol, then developing the theoretical framework linking readout noise to accessible Fisher information, and finally quantifying the improvement achieved by optimizing squeezing parameters.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to AMO physics and quantum optics as it provides a concrete, quantitative method for mitigating measurement-stage noise limitations in superconducting quantum sensors using quantum noise control techniques like squeezing.
